Priya: Observed a deterministic divergence between fp16 and int8 on longprefill runs when RoPE uses a per-token dynamic multiplier that toggles at powers-of-two boundaries. Prefill=96k, cont=single token.

Marco: Can you share the command and the smallest repro?

Priya: run id: rope-boundary-2025-03-12-3
Command:
```bash
./infer_local --model magnet-13b-int8 --ctx 196608 --rope-mode dynamic --rope-toggle-boundaries "powers-of-two" --prefill tests/long_prefill_96k.txt --seed 101
```
Log snippet:
```text
[09:02:01] prefill OK tokens=98304
[09:02:25] rope-toggle applied at token=65536 multiplier=0.75
[09:02:27] first mismatch @65538 fp16='ing' int8='in\n'
```

Eli: Interesting that toggle at 65536 (2^16) triggers mismatch; suggests arithmetic uses 16-bit intermediate somewhere. Did you capture KV index/rotary offsets?

Priya: Yes, KV metadata dumps attached in the artifact. applied_rot_offset shows 65536 but the rotary kernel sees 65534 for a short window. Only in int8 build.

BuildBot: CI job rope-boundary-2025-03-12-3 completed (commit c9d8a7). Artifacts: gs://redwood-ci/rope-boundary/rope-boundary-2025-03-12-3/artifacts.tar.gz

Marco: Could this be a packing/unpacking path that uses uint16 for the multiplier index? Quick test: run with `--rope-mode dynamic --rope-toggle-boundaries none` to verify toggle is the cause.

Priya: With boundaries disabled, no mismatch. With boundaries=primes (toggle at prime token counts) mismatch moves to token 99991, so it's boundary-driven not specifically power-of-two. Strange.

Eli: Hypothesis: some handshake/metadata field storing the toggle index uses varint encoding that previously assumed small values and was truncated in the quantized runtime. Suggest instrumenting the rotary kernel entry to log the incoming rot_offset value per token for the affected range.

Priya: Added instrumentation and saw the sequence: 65534,65535,0,1,... for a short span in the int8 binary only. Looks like a wrap-around because the decoder saw a zero-length prefix decode and interpreted the next bytes as new offset.

Tanya: Mitigation idea: switch handshake encoding to varint with explicit continuation bits (or use fixed 32-bit) and add validation that applied_rot_offset == expected_prefill_total before applying. Also add a decay-tolerant check in the runtime to fallback to fp16 kernel when offsets jump unexpectedly.

Marco: Can we reproduce with a tiny synthetic harness? e.g. prefill N tokens simulated and then emit handshake message with encoded offset. If decoder truncates, we should get same wrap. Priya, can you add that to tests/repro/handshake_sim.py and add to longcontext smoke suite?

Priya: Added repro: tests/repro/handshake_sim.py (flags --encode-varint/--force-truncate). With force-truncate the int8 runtime flips, fp16 unaffected. Pushed artifact and opened PR with unit test.

Eli: For onboarding risk: mark P1, add a canary that forces the handshake to 32-bit on Dedicated until patch lands. Also add a token-by-token comparator in the longcontext CI that fails on any divergence > 1 token difference for prefills > 50k.

BuildBot: Created issue ML-1122 and triggered canary runs with handshake-32bit patch. Canary jobs: dedicated-canary-4.

Tanya: Long-term: move away from implicit tiny encodings for handshake metadata. Use explicit schema with versioning and defensive checks. Also add property-based tests across [1..ctx_max] for handshake encodes/decodes. I'll draft a design note.

Priya: Thanks folks. I'll keep the repro env open and post updated bisect results here. Leaving logs and minimal repro in the artifact link above. :mag:
